newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: World Bank resumes financial aid to Zimbabwe.
newsitem.headline: World Bank resumes financial aid to Zimbabwe.

text.p: The World Bank said on Thursday it was resuming crucial balance-of-payments support to Zimbabwe, two years after withholding aid over the southern African state's failure to implement some cost-cutting measures.

The bank's deputy representative to Zimbabwe Kapil Kapoor told a news conference that the bank "has now advised (the Zimbabwe) government that senior management has approved the release of the second tranche of the second structural adjustment credit worth about $62.5 million".
World bank resumes financial aid to Zimbabwe

Kapoor said the bank had reached the decision last week after reviewing Zimbabwe's macroeconomic performance and its 18-month 1997/98 budget presented on July 24, but only communicated the decision to President Robert Mugabe's government on Wednesday.

"The release of the second tranche had been delayed as a result of macroeconomic uncertainty caused by the fiscal situation. The bank is now of the opinion that good progress has been made in turning the fiscal situation around," he said.
Kapoor said he hoped other Western donors who had withheld balance-of-payments support in 1995 for the same reasons would also now release the money.

World Bank chief representative in Harare David Cook told Reuters last month that on the face of it Zimbabwe's latest budget -- which contained a surprise reduction in the government's spending deficit -- looked good for the release of the $62.5 million balance-of-payments support and general financial support.
